title: Onboarding comparison fieldnotes (Dec 2026)
body:
Purpose and context:
Quick fieldnotes capturing the informal comparisons we ran during the December onboarding window. This is not the final bakeoff report; think of it as the team’s scratchpad + recommendation stub for product and infra about which variant to promote to canary.

Models compared (short names):
- guppy-7b-v2 (FP16 baseline)
- guppy-7b-int4 (4-bit quantized, cerebra quant config)
- canyon-7b-rerank (same params, small reranker head)
- atlas-7b-llm (recent upstream checkpoint, slightly longer context handling)

Prompt sets included (canonical names):
- instr-suite-core-1000: 1k instruction-follow prompts (diverse intents, commercial apps)
- safety-probes-250: targeted safety/hallucination triggers
- convo-robustness-500: multi-turn chat traces from product beta customers
- extractive-q-a-300: short extraction tasks (tables, lists)

What we measured (quick definitions):
- latency_p50/p95: measured at default batch sizing for hosted path on a g4dn-like profile (simulated)
- throughput: tokens/sec under continuous synthetic traffic (100 concurrent sessions)
- instr_f1: human-annotated precision/recall style score on instruction following (0-100 scale)
- hallucination_rate: fraction of outputs with factually incorrect assertions per the safety review rubric
- cost_u: estimated per-million-token cost relative to guppy-7b-v2 baseline (baseline = 1.0)

Condensed leader snapshot (human + infra signals):
Model           p50(ms)  p95(ms)  tput(tok/s)  instr_f1  halluc_rate  cost_u
guippy-7b-v2     48       112      860          86.2      0.071        1.00
guippy-7b-int4  41        98     1030          82.4      0.085        0.68
canyon-7b-rr     53       135      790          88.9      0.062        1.14
atlas-7b-llm     60       170      720          84.7      0.095        1.05

Interpretation notes: 
- Quantized guppy-int4 gives a solid throughput and latency improvement with a non-trivial drop in instr_f1 (~4 points) and a measurable uptick in hallucination cases, particularly on safety-probes and extractive tasks where token-level fidelity matters.
- Canyon-7b-rerank is the best in instruction-following (instr_f1) and lowest hallucination in our sample, but has slightly worse latency and higher cost footprint due to the reranker head. It shines on convo-robustness where multi-turn coherence improved.
- Atlas-7b-llm shows the worst p95 tail and highest hallucination on tabular extraction. Atlas’s strength appears in longer-context summarization (not part of the core promptset we used) — flag for future run.

Pairwise win/loss highlights (informal, per-instruction aggregate):
- canyon vs guppy-v2: canyon wins 58/42 overall, wins strongly on multi-turn and clarification prompts, loses on raw latency-sensitive tasks.
- guppy-int4 vs guppy-v2: guppy-v2 wins 64/36 on extractive and safety probes; int4 wins on raw throughput and cost.
- atlas vs canyon: canyon wins 55/45 on instruction adherence; atlas wins 60/40 on long-context summarization (out-of-scope here).

Selected failure modes observed (examples):
- guppy-int4: numeric truncation on table extraction (lost decimal alignment), hallucinated row names when source table had missing headers.
- canyon-7b-rr: occasional output truncation in streaming mode when reranker handshake delayed token emission (trace attached in linked PR).
- atlas-7b-llm: confidently wrong metadata in Q/A about dates (safety-probes #24, #31).

Prompt-level sensitivities (qualitative):
- instr-suite-core-1000: canyon shows consistent preference for conservative answers (fewer false positives), guppy-int4 drifts to shorter token spans.
- convo-robustness-500: canyon and guppy-v2 both keep context, but canyon issues clarifying questions more reliably.

Decision recommendation (quick):
- Short-term (canary rollout): Promote canyon-7b-rerank to canary for hosted-default route for orgs with medium/high accuracy needs (opt-in default in console). Rationale: best instruction F1 and lowest hallucination; cost/latency tradeoff acceptable for accuracy-first apps.
- Cost-tiered offering: Offer guppy-7b-int4 as a lower-cost "economy" route for customers that opt-in to lower fidelity (clearly labeled in Console with safety caveats).
- Don’t promote atlas-7b-llm yet for default instruction workloads; schedule a longer-context-focused bakeoff for Q1 2027.

Operational asks for infra/ops before canary:
- SRE: confirm streaming handshake fix for canyon reranker (JIRA MLON-798) and add a 2s tail-slashed buffer in gateway to avoid forced truncation.
- Product: surface a cost/quality toggle in Console rollout modal, add inline safety blurb when selecting guppy-int4.
- Applied ML: run a 10k instruction regression pass with adversarially selected prompts (especially numeric/table probes) and produce a regression diff report.

Open questions / risks:
- How sensitive is canyon’s low hallucination signal to larger production-scale traffic patterns (we sampled at 100 concurrent sessions only)?
- Does int4 drift more over time on some long-tail token distributions (observed tiny drift in run #3)? Need longer soak.
- Atlas license / downstream constraints for enterprise customers (legal check for third-party weights).

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Asha: coordinate 10k regression run + updated evaluation harness (due 2026-12-18).
- Marco: queue SRE jitter tests and confirm streaming patch ETA (due 2026-12-14).
- Benji: draft Console UX copy for economy route and safety blurb (due 2026-12-11).
- Sofia: assemble canary rollout checklist and customer-facing FAQ (due 2026-12-15).

Appendix (notes and links):
- Quick method notes: all evals used the local evaluation harness branch ml-eval/dec2026-fieldnotes; seeds fixed where indicated in logs.
- Annotation protocol: 3 annotators per prompt, majority label used for instr_f1. Disagreements labeled for follow-up.
- Raw logs/traces location: see linked github PR and Jira references above.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc bundles quick empirical signals plus operational suggestions. Please comment inline if you want a stricter numeric threshold before canary (proposal was instr_f1 >= 87 to be auto-promoted; canyon is 88.9 so it barely passes).
- If product prefers earlier cost-optimizations, we can pilot guppy-int4 on a small subset of customers and collect quality telemetry for 30 days before wider availability.

End of fieldnotes.
